incidente.resumo: On August 14, 2003, a software bug (a race condition) in the alarm system of FirstEnergy's control room left operators unaware of the need to redistribute load as overloaded transmission lines in the Cleveland-Akron area tripped after tree contact, and a local failure cascaded into a blackout affecting an estimated 55 million people in the Northeastern and Midwestern U.S. and Ontario. Power was restored progressively over 2 hours to 4 days depending on location, with hydro-electric and other plants brought online.
servicos_afetados: electric power grid in parts of the Northeastern and Midwestern United States and Ontario
tecnologias: General Electric Energy XA/21 energy management system

descricao.texto: FirstEnergy operators began to suspect a failure after receiving a notification from American Electric Power (AEP) at 2:32 p.m. about a short AEP line outage for which the FE EMS had failed to raise an alert.
trechos: Operators began to suspect a failure after receiving a notification from American Electric Power (AEP) at 2:32 p.m. about a short AEP line outage that the FE EMS had failed to raise an alert for.

gatilho.texto: Cleveland-Akron area 345 kV transmission lines failed due to tree contact between 3:05 p.m. and 3:42 p.m. (Harding-Chamberlin, then Hanna-Juniper at 3:32 p.m.), followed by the Star-South Canton line at 3:41 p.m. after its loading rose from 82% to 120%, and 138 kV lines between 3:39 p.m. and 4:08 p.m.
trechos: Three 345 kV transmission lines failed between 3:05 p.m. to 3:42 p.m. due to tree contact.
The first was the Harding-Chamberlin line.
Most of the load from that line was transferred to the Hanna-Juniper line, which then failed at 3:32 p.m.
The Star-South Canton line failed at 3:41 p.m. after its loading increased from 82% to 120% after the failure of the Hanna-Juniper line.
Next, the 138 kV lines failed between 3:39 p.m. to 4:08 p.m.

descricao.texto: A race condition bug in General Electric Energy's Unix-based XA/21 energy management system stalled FirstEnergy's control room alarm system for over an hour; operators were unaware of the malfunction and lost audio and visual alerts, leaving them unaware of the need to redistribute load after overloaded transmission lines dropped in voltage.
trechos: A software bug known as a race condition existed in General Electric Energy's Unix-based XA/21 energy management system.
Once triggered, the bug stalled FirstEnergy's control room alarm system for over an hour.
System operators were unaware of the malfunction. The failure deprived them of both audio and visual alerts for important changes in system state.

The blackout was due to a software bug in the alarm system at the control room of FirstEnergy, which rendered operators unaware of the need to redistribute load after overloaded transmission lines dropped in voltage.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: After the alarm system failure, unprocessed events queued up; the primary EMS server failed within 30 minutes and the backup server failed at 14:54, slowing operators' console screen refresh from 1–3 seconds to 59 seconds per screen. A warm reboot at 3:08 p.m. left the alarm function broken, and a cold reboot (later discovered to be the vendor-recommended action) was rejected.
trechos: Unprocessed events queued up after the alarm system failure and the primary server failed within 30 minutes.
Then all applications (including the stalled alarm system) were automatically transferred to the backup server, which itself failed at 14:54.
The server failures slowed the screen refresh rate of the operators' computer consoles from 1–3 seconds to 59 seconds per screen.
IT performed a "warm reboot" of the primary server at 3:08 p.m. but did not realize that the alarm function remained broken.

A "cold reboot"—later discovered to be the vendor-recommended action—was rejected because the power system situation was precarious and operators were concerned about the greater loss of functionality during the reboot procedure.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: MISO's state estimator was inoperative from 12:15 p.m. after incorrect telemetry data (it was not restarted after the telemetry was corrected); when reactivated at 2:40 p.m. its results did not match empirical data because it was unaware of the 2:02 p.m. DPL line outage, and it was modelling correctly again only by 4:04 p.m. The failures in the MISO SE and FE EMS prevented either from recognizing and responding to the line failures.
trechos: 12:15 p.m. Incorrect telemetry data renders the state estimator, a power flow monitoring tool operated by the Indiana-based Midwest Independent Transmission System Operator (MISO), inoperative. An operator corrects the telemetry problem, but forgets to restart the monitoring tool.
The MISO SE was reactivated at 2:40 p.m, but the results confused operators because the model did not match empirical data.
The discrepancy was caused by the SE being unaware of the DPL line outage at 2:02 p.m; DPL's reliability coordinator was PJM, so DPL did not automatically report data to MISO.
MISO operators had the SE modelling correctly again by 4:04 p.m.
The failures in the MISO SE and FE EMS prevented either from recognizing and responding to the failures.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Generation and reactive power resources in the Cleveland-Akron area were reduced: several generators were offline, four or five capacitor banks were offline for routine maintenance, and the Eastlake unit 5 outage at 1:31 p.m. put the FE system at risk of overloads in certain contingency scenarios.
trechos: On August 14, a number of power generators in and around the area were offline.
This reduced the available resources for voltage control and reactive power management in contingencies but did not affect normal operation.

Four or five of the area's capacitor banks—also used to manage reactive power—were also offline for routine maintenance; this did not follow the best practice of performing such maintenance during low-demand periods, and their status was not reported for regional planning purposes because FE had deemed them to be non-critical infrastructure.
In the Cleveland-Akron area, Eastlake Power Plant unit 5 went offline at 1:31 p.m.
However, the loss of the Eastlake unit put the FE system at risk of overloads in certain contingency scenarios; FE did not notice the danger.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The task force final report lists inadequate management of tree growth in FirstEnergy's transmission rights-of-way among the causes; high heat increased energy demand and made power lines sag as higher currents heated them.
trechos: FirstEnergy "failed to manage adequately tree growth in its transmission rights-of-way."
Much of the affected region reached temperatures higher than 31 °C (88 °F) that day, increasing energy demand as people across the region turned on fans and air conditioning.
This caused the power lines to sag as higher currents heated the lines.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Neighboring entities had incomplete information: FE did not notify MISO of its degraded situational awareness, MISO and FirstEnergy controllers did not inform system controllers in nearby states, and PJM and AEP had incomplete data on FE's system and underestimated the severity.
trechos: FE failed to notify MISO of its degraded situational awareness.
While MISO and FirstEnergy controllers concentrate on understanding the failures, they fail to inform system controllers in nearby states.

PJM and AEP began mitigation efforts to prevent the Star-South Canton line connecting FE and AEP from overloading; they had incomplete data on the status of FE's system and underestimated the severity of the situation.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The task force final report also lists among the causes that FirstEnergy and its reliability council failed to assess and understand the inadequacies of FE's system, particularly voltage instability and the vulnerability of the Cleveland-Akron area, and the failure of the interconnected grid's reliability organizations to provide effective real-time diagnostic support.
trechos: FirstEnergy (FE) and its reliability council "failed to assess and understand the inadequacies of FE's system, particularly with respect to voltage instability and the vulnerability of the Cleveland-Akron area
failure of the interconnected grid's reliability organizations to provide effective real-time diagnostic support.

passos.texto: All available hydro-electric plants, and a number of coal- and oil-fired plants, were brought online, bringing some power to areas immediately surrounding the plants by the morning of August 15; much of the nuclear power stayed offline until those plants could be slowly taken out of "safe mode".
trechos: This put much of the nuclear power offline until those plants could be slowly taken out of "safe mode".

In the meantime, all available hydro-electric plants (as well as a number of coal- and oil-fired plants) were brought online, bringing some electrical power to the areas immediately surrounding the plants by the morning of August 15.

passos.texto: Orrville, Ohio, restored power within an hour by disconnecting the local utility from the larger grid and restarting the coal-fired generator.
trechos: Orrville, Ohio, was able to restore power within an hour disconnecting the local utility from the larger grid and restarting the coal-fired generator.

passos.texto: For two days of the recovery period, diversion of water from the Niagara River for hydroelectric generation was increased to the maximum level.
trechos: For two days of this recovery period, diversion of water from the Niagara River for hydroelectric generation was increased to the maximum level, normally used only at night and in winter in order to maintain the scenic appearance of Niagara Falls.

acoes.texto: Already done: the U.S. federal government included reliability provisions in the Energy Policy Act of 2005, and the standards of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation became mandatory for U.S. electricity providers.
trechos: The blackout prompted the federal government of the United States to include reliability provisions in the Energy Policy Act of 2005.
The standards of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation became mandatory for U.S. electricity providers.

motivo_confianca_baixa: deteccao.forma: terceiros vs alerta_automatico. The definition asks how the problem was 'first noticed'; the text says operators began to suspect a failure after AEP's notification at 2:32 p.m. (terceiros), and also that FE IT was automatically notified of the remote terminal and server failures (alerta_automatico) without giving a time, so the definition does not decide which came first.
observacoes: The text gives the duration only as '2 hours–4 days, depending on location' (most places restored by midnight, within 7 hours; full power to New York City and parts of Toronto on August 16), so duracao is null. The text is inconsistent about the AEP contact: one passage says operators began to suspect a failure after AEP's 2:32 p.m. notification, another says the lack of alarms led operators to dismiss a call from AEP. The timeline notes that later analysis suggests the blackout could have been averted before the 4:05:57 p.m. Sammis-Star line trip by cutting 1.5 GW of load in the Cleveland–Akron area. The prevention items are actions by the U.S. federal government, not commitments of FirstEnergy or General Electric.
